label: v/w/l/n/s or <DEL> input after a context of m/r/j/p/k/y/b/0 letters
explanation: Fires almost only in the input phase and at the delimiter, essentially never during copy (0.3% of mass) and never at t<2. The trigger token set is sharp: <DEL> (44% of mass) and the letters v, w, l, n, s (about 53%); these cover 97% of activation mass, mostly on the first occurrence of the token. But only about 6% of trigger-token steps fire, so firing is gated by context. It is more likely, and larger, when the prefix holds many of m, r, j, p, k, y, b, 0 (high-lift first_tok/prev2_tok values) and few earlier v/w/l/n/s; later positions and longer L (L=9 carries 42% of mass) push it up. The largest activations are v/w late in a 9-token input, often followed by a strong <DEL> activation. The context condition looks like a graded accumulation over many tokens, and a count threshold only approximates it, so precision and recall stay around 0.3-0.4 (dev F1 0.34, mass recall 0.48). It does not fire on digits 1-3, vowels, or letters like q, x, c, i, u as inputs.
